review.material: All eight pages of the author-hosted 1998 ICM reading copy read.
review.limitations: The exposition is a proof sketch and historical survey, not an independently checked proof. Its statements about unproved extensions describe the period of writing.

evidence.description: Numerical clues, modular functions and trace series
Four-step proof sketch and denominator identities

sections.title: What this survey asks
sections.text: Why should Monster representations and modular functions share numerical information? The survey turns a surprising coefficient match into a structural question.

sections.title: The key distinction
sections.text: Matching dimensions alone is weak: even trivial actions can have chosen dimensions. Moonshine concerns traces of every Monster element on a specific graded module and the resulting genus-zero functions.

sections.title: Proof architecture
sections.text: Start with the Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman vertex algebra. Apply the no-ghost theorem to construct the Monster Lie algebra. Twisted denominator identities constrain trace coefficients; modular-function results identify the series.

sections.title: Example and outcome
sections.text: The classes 2A and 2B have different trace series despite both containing involutions. Coefficient recurrences connect Lie-algebra structure to modular behavior, going beyond isolated numerical coincidences.

sections.title: What remains historical
sections.text: Later pages discuss generalized and modular moonshine and Dynkin-diagram observations. Their then-open status is not a current research-status claim.
